gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on a two-screen 15.6-inch extender "plug and play, no driver" means one video output per screen (two video-capable ports on the laptop), while "one cable for both screens" means a driver install; Aura's own 15.6-inch pair shows it: the $329 Dual Go Max needs two video outputs and no software, the $409 Dual Boost Pro Max Slim needs one USB-C cable and a driver.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages (itechguides '15 Best', deskgearhq) and the uncited theofficejournal 15.6, workcocoon 15.6 and twelvetabs pages. deskgearhq writes that every configuration, including the two-screen Trio 3 Pro, connects over a single USB-C cable with no driver requirement, and never counts ports per screen. itechguides only relays one Amazon listing's 'driver installation required' for an adapter path. twelvetabs has part of it: it says one Amazon dual 15.6 needs a DisplayLink driver and another does not, but does not tie that to how many video outputs the laptop needs. theofficejournal and workcocoon list only single 15.6-inch monitors and no driver information. None normalises the word 'dual' (one added screen at Mobile Pixels, two at Aura and FOPO).
decides: It confirms a split pick rather than one winner. A 15.6-inch laptop with two video outputs (video-capable USB-C plus HDMI, or two USB-C) can take a driver-free pair of 15.6-inch screens, which is where our FOPO S10 sits by its 'Plug & Play' title and our record, against Aura's Dual Go Max at $329. A laptop with one video-capable USB-C port needs either a one-cable driver model (Aura Dual Boost Pro Max 15.6 Slim, $409) or a single added screen (Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS, USB-C or Mini HDMI, no driver). I could not re-read the S10 page today (HTTP 429), so its video path must be re-sourced from FOPO's page or manual before the table states it.

findings.label: Panel geometry against a 15.6-inch 16:9 laptop screen (arithmetic)
findings.source_title: Tempered Glass Screen Protector – Aura Displays (lists 14", 15.6", 16", 18.5" in 16:9 or 16:10)
findings.note: Computed, not a maker figure: width = diagonal × 16/√337 (16:9) or × 16/√356 (16:10); PPI = √(h² + v²) / diagonal. A 16-inch 16:10 extender panel is the same width as a 15.6-inch laptop panel, 21 mm taller, at the same pixel density, so text matches at 100% scaling. A 14.1-inch 1080p panel is 33 mm narrower and 18 mm shorter and draws the same text about 10% smaller. Which products carry which diagonal and resolution comes from Dealectric's records for the 16-inch and 14-inch rows; I re-read only the S10 (15.6", 1080p) and Duex Max DS (14.1") today.
